title: Deep learning on lung-screening CT estimates spirometry in two external cohorts
summary: A three-dimensional convolutional neural network trained on 10,371 low-dose CT reconstructions from 5,975 NLST participants was fused with 20 densitometry and tracheal geometry features to predict FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. Applied frozen to an external screening cohort (n = 268) and COPDGene (10,302 scans), it detected abnormal spirometry with AUROC 0.898 and 0.913, and concordance correlation coefficients were 0.80-0.88. Agreement was lower with overestimation in a COPD subgroup, the reference spirometry differed (pre- versus post-bronchodilator), and prospective utility is unproven.
ai_technology: 3D convolutional neural network fused with CT-derived densitometry and tracheal features, predicting FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC
organization: University of Florida; D’Or Institute for Research and Education

evidence.tested: A frozen model was evaluated on two external cohorts (n = 268 and 10,302 scans) against reference spirometry.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical utility; performance across populations, since sensitivity and specificity differed at the same decision rule; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A 3D CNN plus quantitative CT features estimated spirometric parameters from existing chest CT.
